subject: Post-demo: model slate recommendations for latency-sensitive POC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Porter <sam@greenbridge.com>, Avery Nash <avery.nash@greenbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Jul 2029 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model slate recommendations for latency-sensitive POC

Hi Sam / Avery —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. As promised, below is a concise post-demo recap and our recommended candidate slate for your latency-sensitive POC (three options with tradeoffs). I focused the list on models that maintain high relevance on clinical-text prompts while keeping tail latency and token cost predictable under 100ms median inference for short prompts (up to 256 tokens).

Quick recap:
- Goal: integrate short clinical-reply generation into triage UI with 200ms 95th percentile target, preserve hallucination controls for medication and care-plan mentions.
- Dataset: your 5k de-identified triage examples (thanks for sharing).
- Constraints: strict PII handling (VPC/private deploy preferred), limited ops runway for quantization work.

Recommended slate (shortlist + rationale) — prioritized by our recommended sequence for pilot:

1) Lumen-7B-q4f16 (quantized) — Recommended pilot start
  - Why: Best latency/cost balance for short prompts; runs well on 1xA10-like instance with our q4f16 path.
  - Latency: median ≈ 40–55ms, p95 ≈ 140–180ms (single-request, no prefix cache).
  - Cost: ~0.6x of Atlas-13B for per-token inference cost.
  - Quality: strong factuality on short clinical completions; occasional omission on multi-step instructions.
  - Ops: minimal quantization tuning required; fits in our dedicated pod with standard KV cache.

2) Atlas-13B-fp16 — Conservative fallback for accuracy
  - Why: Higher QA pass rate on structured clinical prompts where ordering and subtle negations matter.
  - Latency: median ≈ 90–120ms, p95 ≈ 260–350ms (higher CPU tail without batching).
  - Cost: ~1.6x of Lumen-7B-q4f16.
  - Quality: fewer omissions and better multi-step reasoning, preferred when hallucination risk is critical.
  - Ops: requires 2x GPU capacity compared to Lumen; good candidate for canary → slow roll.

3) Nimbus-34B-8bit — High-quality, last-resort option for complex threads
  - Why: Highest fidelity across long context and edge-case medical discourse; use only where downstream checks demand highest recall/precision.
  - Latency: median ≈ 220–300ms, p95 > 600ms unless aggressive batching; not suitable for strict 200ms SLO.
  - Cost: ~4–5x of Lumen.
  - Quality: best across all our eval sets but operationally expensive.
  - Ops: recommend as regional fallback for off-peak heavy-compute runs.

Suggested rollout plan (to hit your 200ms p95 target while preserving quality):
- Phase A (Week 1): Pilot Lumen-7B-q4f16 in VPC private deployment with prefix caching enabled for common triage templates. Collect token-level latency and QA metrics.
- Phase B (Week 2–3): Canary Atlas-13B-fp16 for 10% of traffic where prompts include medication mentions or multi-step instructions. Monitor hallucination rate and false positives.
- Phase C (Week 4): Enable Nimbus-34B-8bit as on-demand batch processing for complex logs / offline re-runs.

Quality/regression concerns and mitigations:
- Regression risk: quantized Lumen variant may drop on rare syntactic negations — we propose a 20-prompt negative-avoidance probe set (included in prompt_pack).
- Monitoring: run both a semantic-similarity threshold and a facts-extraction check (extracted entities compared to pattern-based NER) on every response; alert if "medication_mismatch_rate" increases >1.5x baseline.
- Guardrails: deploy a two-step verification flow where any medication mention triggers a secondary conservative call (Atlas-13B) if confidence score < 0.75.

Benchmarks and artifacts attached: greenbridge_benchmarks_20290721.csv (latency/cost/QA breakdown), prompt_pack_greenbridge_v1.zip (probes, canonical prompts, negative examples), canary-playbook.md (rollout steps + rollback criteria).

Ask / next steps:
- Can you confirm which AWS region you prefer for the VPC private deployment? (us-west-2 preferred by ops)
- If acceptable, we’ll provision a 2-week pilot for Lumen-7B-q4f16 and share a telemetry dashboard link within 24 hours.

If you want, Ben can join a short 30-minute call to walk through the rollout plan and the canary playbook.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Marissa —

This is great, thank you. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the pilot: 
1) Region: us-west-2 works for us.
2) For the canary rule you suggested (medication mentions → trigger Atlas), can you confirm whether that doubles the per-request latency for those flows? We need to size UX impact.
3) Is there a quick way to sandbox the negative-avoidance probe set against our supplied 5k examples?

Prefer a quick sync tomorrow morning if possible. Avery and I are available 10:00–11:00 PT.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Porter <sam@greenbridge.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Jul 2029 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model slate recommendations for latency-sensitive POC

Sam — quick answers so the team can plan sizing: 
- Medication-triggered fallback (Lumen -> Atlas): We implement an asynchronous pattern where we return Lumen's suggestion immediately and in parallel run a quick Atlas check for any medication token matches. If Atlas flags a mismatch, UI shows a safe-edit overlay. Practically: median latency for primary response ~50ms; the Atlas verification adds verification latency for the UI overlay only when mismatch triggers — no full double-block on every call. Expected p95 impact for the small subset (~8% of calls) is +120–180ms when the overlay path is taken.
- Sandbox: yes — we can run the negative-avoidance probe set over your 5k examples in our eval cluster. That will produce a CSV with per-prompt flags (false-negation, hallucination-score) — I attached the sample results in the benchmarks CSV.

If you want us to call out exact UX impact numbers for marketing/legal review, we can run an A/B test during week 1 of the pilot and provide concrete latency distributions for the medication flow.

Ben
Ben Carter | Solution Lead, Redwood Inference
